record.title: Hunan report describes early site work for a planned 1,500P green-power compute center
record.summary: A Hunan MIIT report dated 2026-02-11 says land-leveling work was underway at the planned Zhiliang Xinghe Intelligent Cloud Computing Center site after a land transfer on 2025-12-11. It describes a planned RMB 5.2 billion investment, 1,500P of intelligent compute and a green-power direct-supply/compute-integration design. These are project plans and a dated early-site-work account, not evidence that the center is complete or operating.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Hunan's Industry and Information Technology Department published a 2026-02-11 report stating that land-leveling work was underway at the planned Zhiliang Xinghe Intelligent Cloud Computing Center site and that the land transfer had been completed on 2025-12-11.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The report describes a planned RMB 5.2 billion project with 1,500P of intelligent compute and calls it Hunan's first provincial green-power direct-supply and compute-integration project.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The February report does not establish current construction progress, completion, operating capacity, green-power delivery, utilization, cost, reliability or compute-service outcomes.

evidence_gaps.description: No newer first-party dated project update, official tender record or commissioning notice was retrieved after the February early-site-work account.
The planned capacity and green-power design have no inspected commissioning, utilization, grid-delivery or price records.
No independent evidence measures power cost, reliability, emissions or useful compute service for the project.

brief.importance_rationale: If built to the reported scope, a RMB 5.2 billion project planned for 1,500P of intelligent compute and direct green-power supply would be a meaningful regional compute-infrastructure investment. The official report establishes only land transfer and early site work as of February 2026; construction completion, operating capacity, electricity delivery and utilization remain unknown.
limitations: The source is an official report from February 2026 and does not establish the project's status in October 2026.
RMB 5.2 billion, 1,500P capacity and green-power integration are reported project plans, not measured operational facts.
No commissioning, available capacity, utilization, electricity delivery, tariff, reliability, storage dispatch, emissions or useful-compute output was inspected.
A separate third-party tender listing with different facility specifications was not verified against a first-party procurement record; no identity or scope reconciliation is claimed here.
The July Hunan compute-supplier registration rules do not show that this project registered or qualified as a supplier.

technical.claimed_result: The official report describes a planned 1,500P center and says site leveling was underway; it provides no operating performance data.
technical.demonstrated_result: The Hunan MIIT report was published on 2026-02-11 and states that land leveling was underway and the land transfer had been completed on 2025-12-11. the research desk did not verify the site or later status independently.
technical.mechanism: The planned facility is described as combining intelligent-compute infrastructure with direct green-power supply. The inspected report does not specify grid topology, storage operation, delivered energy or compute utilization.
technical.regime: One Hunan provincial government report dated 2026-02-11 about early site work for a planned 1,500P compute center with reported RMB 5.2 billion investment.
technical.strongest_baseline: No operating baseline or matched energy/cost comparison was reported or inspected; no performance effect is claimed.

brief.title: Hunan report describes early site work for a planned 1,500P green-power compute center
brief.why_it_matters: Large compute deployments depend on both power supply and site infrastructure. The official report documents an early construction milestone for a high-capacity Hunan project intended to combine compute with direct green-power supply. The reported investment and capacity remain plans, and the report provides no current construction inspection or operational measurements.
